target_customer: Online advertisers and publishers using an ad network that targeted by user feedback; later consumers looking for apps
problem: Ad targeting relied on crude contextual or behavioral signals. Hello Chair built a recommendation engine (SparseReduce) that used explicit user feedback to personalize ads, then reused it for app discovery.
business_model: ad network revenue share (Adpinion), later an app discovery platform (Appsaurus)
product_category: machine learning ad network and recommendation engine

founders.name: Luke Iannini
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in the company bio on the YC page; education and employers not found in a source I opened.

founders.name: Mike Jacobs
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as Michael Jacobs.

competitors.name: Advertising.com
competitors.what: Largest ad network by reach, the incumbent for display advertising
competitors.traction_then: Reached 87 percent of online Americans in May 2007 per comScore as reported by ClickZ
competitors.funding_then: Owned by AOL by then, not verified in the cited page

competitors.name: ValueClick
competitors.what: Large ad network ranked among the top networks by reach
competitors.traction_then: Ranked in the May 2007 ClickZ top 50 ad network list

technical_complexity.rationale: A recommendation engine for sparse feedback data at ad-serving scale was research-flavored machine learning for a small team in 2007.

defensibility.rationale: The algorithm was the only asset, and ad networks compete on publisher and advertiser supply that a two-year-old startup lacked.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes an incumbent response. The company is listed as inactive with no sale found.

market_need_then: Display ad networks were consolidating in 2007 and targeting quality was a selling point, but no source shows demand for Adpinion specifically.

branding.domain_note: hellochair.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page (checked 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: The company bio is playful in tone, for example calling Appsaurus the subject of overwhelming critical acclaim, per the YC page.

branding.brand_signature: Appsaurus product name (dinosaur pun), trademarked by Hello Chair Inc.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand or community found; the company name did not describe the product and the domain is now parked.

pivots.to: Appsaurus app discovery platform built on SparseReduce
pivots.why: Company bio says SparseReduce was applied to many recommendation problems; Appsaurus was released on the eve of 2010.

outcome_analysis: Hello Chair started as an applied machine learning company, shipped an ad network in 2007 and by 2010 pivoted to an app discovery product on the same engine. It raised a tiny YC seed and about 880 thousand dollars in 2010 per one database, and is now listed inactive. No source states a cause of failure, so the pivot_failed label is an inference from the timeline and the cause is not public.
notes: Both rounds rest on a single aggregator (startupintros); Dealroom shows the 880K round as Seed and the aggregator labels it Series U, so stage is other. Kando lists YC and Chris Sacca as seed investors and Mitch Kapor as an initial investor; Seedtable shows none and Crunchbase shows one round. The 2010 round amount and investors beyond Harrison Metal are unverified. Competitors listed are generic large networks from a 2007 ranking, no direct rival to Adpinion was found. Website was a parked domain; the YC page was fetched; no shutdown cause found.
